verdict.rationale: cubic's docs say that once installed it automatically reviews new pull requests and comments on bugs and improvements. Its feedback draws on codebase context, cross-repo links and learnings from senior reviewers' past comments. Hands-on community reports back up the contextual quality: one user found it contextualizes the app where other tools stayed surface level, and a months-long tester found it quieter and more useful. Missing for 10: PRs opened before installation need a manual `@cubic-dev-ai review this PR` trigger, and only GitHub is evidenced, with no GitLab support.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get automatic code review with contextual feedback on every pull request

citations.quote: Once installed, cubic automatically reviews new pull requests.
Comments on bugs and improvements in pull requests
Link related repositories so reviews can check shared APIs, schemas, docs, or release work.
cubic analyzes their historical PR comments to extract learnings from the patterns they consistently enforce.
Some of the other tools I tried didn't seem to contextualize the app, so the comments were surface level and trite.
I've been testing this for the last few months, and it is now much quieter than before, and even more useful.
